A1.justification: Both complete, readable 24-page PDFs describe MMLANDMARKS and its MMCLIP baseline. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C can be matched, including the exchanged positions of Figures 10 and 11.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-view retrieval, geolocalization, text retrieval, and ablation results in Tables 2–6, plus dataset analyses and a 1,000-image filtering audit in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses, adds evaluated comparators, and reports revised text-retrieval results.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the CLIP image/text encoders, GeoCLIP-style location encoder, two-layer projection heads, pairwise InfoNCE objective, and nearest-neighbor inference. Appendix Algorithm 1 also remains unchanged. Text-query redaction changes evaluation inputs, not the proposed model.

E1.justification: The same US landmarks, modalities, and retrieval/geolocalization tasks remain. However, Section 5.3 revises the text-query scenario: v1 uses first sentences that may explicitly identify locations, whereas v2 evaluates sentences with place names removed, changing the information available for localization.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens geolocalization comparisons: TransGeo-90°FoV enters cross-view retrieval and indirect geolocalization; G3 and GeoReasoner enter both ground and satellite geolocalization; SatCLIP enters satellite geolocalization. Tables 2–4 therefore evaluate additional relevant approaches, including LLM/VLM methods, while retaining previous comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 introduces GPT-3.5 processing and manual editing to remove explicit location cues before text evaluation. The satellite/GPS gallery is now reported as 101,000 entries including query locations, versus 100,000 previously, and the ground-query count changes from 18,689 to 18,688. These establish revised reported settings, without establishing that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Table 6 retains the same objective, modality, sentence-sampling, aerial-sampling, and outdoor-filtering ablations. Appendix distribution analyses, VLM error inspection, and temporal case studies also remain. Text redaction replaces the main evaluation protocol rather than adding a separate controlled ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark results. The appendix's 1,000-image manual audit and its reporting procedure are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 5 replaces the text-task results: MMCLIP Text-to-Satellite mAP@1k changes from 36.2 to 17.3, and Text-to-GPS accuracy within 1 km changes from 17.6% to 4.2%. These use revised evaluation conditions and cannot establish a same-setting performance decline. Tables 2–4 add comparator results; their previously reported rows and Table 6 retain their printed scores.

T1.justification: Equation 1 retains the same averaging of pairwise contrastive losses, and Appendix Algorithm 1 retains the same collection logic. No substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The dataset and multitask contributions remain. The abstract and conclusion narrow the emphasis from competing with or outperforming specialized models to demonstrating versatility and the value of multimodal training. Section 5 explicitly states that MMCLIP's performance is not intended to establish model superiority.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies comparisons between trained MMCLIP and zero-shot models, explains city-center prediction limitations and SatCLIP's imagery-domain mismatch, and extends the possible MP16-overlap concern to G3. Text-task interpretation changes from strong results aided by geographic cues to weaker performance from less informative, redacted sentences.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents query-landmark sampling, latest-aerial query selection, city-name-to-coordinate conversion, and text-redaction procedures. It reports training-only indoor/outdoor counts rather than whole-dataset counts. Conversely, Section 4 drops the explicit ViT-L/14 specification and GPS-encoder trainability statement; hardware and numerical training hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a localized discussion of LLM/VLM geolocalization citing G3, GeoRanker, GeoReasoner, and GAEA. Language-model and event-detection references are also added, while the standalone ViT reference is removed. The broader positioning around multimodal, instance-level geospatial data remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, related-work passages, experimental framing and discussion, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. v2 adds a Query set paragraph and acknowledgements, reorganizes implementation prose, and expands author names. These edits substantially revise the narrative despite retaining the main section sequence and appendix organization.

P2.justification: Tables 2–5 gain zero-shot labels, Tables 2–4 gain comparator rows, and Tables 3–4 are rearranged. Figure 1 updates map markers and example coordinates; Figure 3 is resized. Figure 2 moves earlier, and appendix Figures 10 and 11 exchange positions and numbering without adding visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the credibility of the evaluation by removing explicit geographic shortcuts from text queries, adding relevant comparators, and qualifying claims based on comparisons between trained MMCLIP and zero-shot models. Query and gallery documentation also becomes clearer. These focused gains outweigh the loss of some implementation specificity, while the underlying dataset, method, and most experimental evidence remain unchanged.
